questions.prompt: Three CSVs `Customers_Part1/2/3.csv` share identical fields. The ONE-tool way to read all three at once is:
options: Input Data with a wildcard path: Customers_*.csv
A Join tool with three inputs
questions.explain: **Wildcard in Input Data** works when files share fields/types. Alternative: 3 × Input Data → **Union** (Auto Config by Name). Then **Unique** on Customer ID — **U anchor** = uniques, **D anchor** = duplicates (the D count answers 'how many duplicates').

questions.source: Challenge S1.2 — sheets + nulls + anchor trap
questions.prompt: Orders for 2021/2022 sit on separate Excel SHEETS. After listing sheet names, which tool streams every sheet as one table?
options: Dynamic Input (template = one sheet; read list of Sheet Names; Change File/Table Name)
questions.explain: Input Data with **<List of Sheet Names>** → **Dynamic Input** stacks all sheets. Then **Imputation** (Null() → Median) fixes Quantity, and the Filter 'Status Equals Cancelled' — ⚠ continue from the **F anchor** to KEEP non-cancelled (the classic anchor trap).

questions.prompt: After Join (orders ↔ Products.csv on Product ID), rows on the **L anchor** are:
options: Orders whose Product ID has NO match in Products.csv (unknown products)
questions.explain: **J** = matched both sides · **L** = left-only (orders with unknown products) · **R** = right-only (products never ordered). Mentioning what the L rows MEAN is where the marks hide.

questions.prompt: Which Alteryx formula function returns whole days between Ship Date and Order Date? (function name only)
questions.explain: `DateTimeDiff([Ship Date],[Order Date],"days")` → Int. Then the Shipping Status formula: IF actual = scheduled THEN "Shipped On Time" ELSEIF actual > scheduled THEN "Shipped Late" ELSE "Shipped Early" ENDIF — finished with **Summarize** (GroupBy Region + Status, Count).

questions.prompt: EduFunGames has columns January_Sales … December_Sales that must become ROWS (month, value). Which tool, and what's its inverse?
options: Transpose (Key: Product+Category; Data: the 12 month columns) — inverse is Cross Tab
Cross Tab — inverse is Transpose... the other way round
questions.explain: **Transpose** = wide→long (Name/Value columns appear). **Cross Tab** = long→wide (group rows, header column, value aggregation) — the inverse pair. Cross Tab quirk: output columns sort alphabetically.

questions.prompt: `Address` holds "2316 E 5th Ave, Denver, CO 80206-4205". To get Street/City/StateZip columns:
options: Text To Columns — delimiter ',' — Split to 3 Columns
questions.explain: **Text To Columns**, comma delimiter, 3 columns → rename in a **Select**. Output Data path trick for a named Excel sheet: `BizRecords_Clean.xlsx|||Mailing` (the `|||sheet` syntax).

questions.source: Challenge S1.7 — string cleaning (where marks hide)
questions.prompt: Sales arrive as strings like `"$3,101 "`. A Select-tool conversion to Double yields nulls. The working recipe is:
questions.explain: Strip **$** and **,** with nested ReplaceString, Trim spaces, THEN ToNumber → Double. The Select tool alone cannot strip characters — this cleaning step is exactly 'where marks hide' per the solutions.

questions.prompt: "Average units of the 10 largest Casual Dining chains by sales" — the tool chain is:
options: Filter (SEGMENT = Casual Dining) → Sort (Sales desc) → Sample (First 10) → Summarize (Avg Units)
questions.explain: Filter the segment → **Sort descending** → **Sample First N = 10** → **Summarize Avg**. Memorize this top-N idiom; assessments recycle it.

questions.prompt: To produce a titled PDF of a summary table, the Alteryx reporting chain is:
options: Table → Report Header (title + date) → Render (Output Mode = PDF)
questions.explain: **Table** styles the grid → **Report Header** adds title/date → **Render** writes the PDF. Note Summarize GroupBy sorts alphabetically (April, August, February…) — that IS the expected output order.
